title: AST SpaceMobile's Brazil Deal Could Be a Major Growth Catalyst
author: Rick Orford
description: AST SpaceMobile has taken a significant step toward commercial service in Brazil, potentially creating a blueprint for growth across other markets. However, Amazon's acquisition of Globalstar brings fresh competition as ASTS stock struggles to recover from a steep sell-off. The company's next major catalyst may depend on delivering operational gateways, reliable coverage, and paying customers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company has achieved a positive milestone with Brazil expansion, but faces significant headwinds including a steep stock sell-off (-15.22%), missed satellite deployment targets (45 satellites), and intensifying competition from Amazon. The outlook is mixed with potential upside dependent on execution.
Amazon's acquisition of Globalstar represents a competitive threat to AST SpaceMobile's satellite communications business, raising stakes and potentially limiting ASTS's market opportunities.
Globalstar was acquired by Amazon, which validates the strategic value of satellite communications assets and positions the company within a well-capitalized tech giant.

title: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold ASTS Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
author: Na
description: AST SpaceMobile is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on Nov. 9 with estimated revenues of $44.4 million and a loss of 41 cents per share. The company benefits from satellite constellation expansion, growing MNO partnerships covering 3 billion subscribers, and a $1.3 billion revenue backlog. However, high capital expenditures ($350-425M expected in Q3), launch risks, and intense competition from SpaceX's Starlink and Globalstar pose significant challenges. The stock has underperformed the industry by 46.9% over the past year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed outlook with positive fundamentals (expanding constellation, $1.3B backlog, 60+ MNO partnerships) offset by significant headwinds (46.9% stock decline, high capex requirements, launch risks, competitive pressure, negative earnings surprises). Zacks Rank #3 with negative ESP of -15.86% suggests no earnings beat expected.
Identified as a peer that has significantly outperformed ASTS, with stock surging 78.6% over the past year, demonstrating stronger market performance in the satellite communications sector.

title: Can ASTS' Handoff Test With AT&T Strengthen Its Growth Prospects?
author: Na
description: AST SpaceMobile successfully demonstrated seamless handoffs between terrestrial cellular and satellite networks in collaboration with AT&T, with support from Ericsson and Nokia. The achievement marks progress toward commercial deployment of direct-to-device satellite connectivity through BlueBird satellites, aimed at extending coverage to remote areas. However, ASTS shares have underperformed significantly, trading at a premium valuation while earnings estimates have declined.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the technical achievement of seamless network handoffs is positive and represents progress toward commercialization, this is offset by significant negative factors: 47.2% share price decline over the past year, valuation trading at 6x industry average (P/S of 27.98 vs 4.65), and declining earnings estimates (2026 and 2027 estimates both worsened). The company carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

AT&T's involvement in the demonstration is collaborative and supportive of satellite connectivity expansion, but this represents a minor partnership development with limited direct impact on AT&T's core business operations.

title: Can ASTS Turn Brazil's Spectrum Approval Into a Growth Opportunity?
author: Na
description: AST SpaceMobile received spectrum authorization from Brazil's telecom regulator to operate satellite-based mobile services, gaining access to 30 MHz of S-band spectrum and up to 20 MHz of 700 MHz spectrum. The company plans to invest in four ground gateways to connect its BlueBird satellites with existing mobile networks, targeting underserved areas across Brazil's 210+ million population. However, ASTS shares have declined 48% over the past year and trade at a significantly elevated valuation multiple compared to industry peers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the Brazil spectrum approval represents a positive business development and expansion opportunity, this is offset by significant headwinds: 48% share price decline over the past year, valuation trading at 6.5x industry average (P/S of 30.26 vs 4.64), and declining earnings estimates for 2026-2027. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

Globalstar received FCC approval for its next-generation C-3 satellite system supporting direct-to-smartphone connectivity and has launched eight HIBLEO-4 replacement satellites to strengthen its low Earth orbit network, demonstrating technological advancement and regulatory progress.

Viasat is actively expanding satellite communication capabilities with operational ViaSat-3 satellites serving multiple regions and developing advanced technology to improve data transmission and network capacity for broadband and mobility services.

title: ASTS' Bottom Line Plummets: Should You Stay Cautious About the Stock?
author: Na
description: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) has experienced a sharp 43.7% decline over the past year due to mounting losses, high operating expenses, and execution challenges. The company recorded a $125.9M loss from its BlueBird 7 launch failure and faces intense competition from Starlink and Globalstar. Despite plans to deploy 45-60 satellites by end of 2026, negative estimate revisions and geopolitical uncertainties have prompted a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company faces significant headwinds including 43.7% stock decline, $125.9M loss from BlueBird 7 launch setback, widened loss estimates for 2026-2027, high operating expenses, launch dependency risks, and intense competition from better-capitalized competitors like SpaceX's Starlink. Zacks assigned a Sell rating.
